links.outcome: Errors in benchmark calculator implementations and ground truth
links.effect: Audit identified and fixed over 20 errors, from critical formula inaccuracies to runtime bugs; residual model errors attributed mainly to ground-truth issues and dataset ambiguities.
links.quote: First, we conduct a systematic audit of the benchmark's calculator implementations, identifying and fixing over 20 errors ranging from critical formula inaccuracies to runtime bugs in a NeurIPS-published dataset.

links.outcome: Accuracy on clinical calculator tasks with vs without calculator specification in prompt
links.effect: Providing the calculator specification at inference (open-book) raised accuracy from ~52% to 81-85% on GLM-4.6V and GLM-4.7, without fine-tuning.
links.quote: Second, we show that a simple intervention-providing the model with the calculator specification at inference time ("open-book" prompting)-raises accuracy from ~52% to 81-85% on GLM-4.6V and GLM-4.7, surpassing all published results including RL-trained systems, without any fine-tuning.

links.outcome: LLM accuracy on clinical calculation tasks under direct prompting
links.effect: State-of-the-art direct prompting scores plateau around 35% on the Verified split; the study concludes the benchmark measures formula memorization and arithmetic precision.
links.quote: MedCalc-Bench is a widely used benchmark for evaluating LLM performance on clinical calculator tasks, with state-of-the-art direct prompting scores plateauing around 35% on the Verified split (HELM MedHELM leaderboard) and the best published approach-RL with verifiable rewards-reaching 74%.
